investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T22:15–22:22Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster has zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads — 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner collected no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), causing every contract assertion to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production-api cluster. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have exhausted their allocatable quota; the remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. With no preemption victims available, the pod remained Unschedulable for ~144–147 seconds until the eval timeout fired. This is a cluster-capacity or node-affinity configuration problem in the production runtime, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of impact to other features or user traffic is present in the supplied packet.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots on the two kata-peerpods-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node label drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the required node labels or taints expected by the remote-agent pod spec, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity problem.

QUATERNARY — Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from a prior run consuming the remaining VM slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) failed on a previous run, orphaned pods may be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and preventing new scheduling.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and the affinity/selector mismatch or a pod spec error would need to be investigated instead.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and collects all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes are found to carry the required labels and the pod spec's nodeAffinity/nodeSelector is misconfigured, the root cause shifts from capacity exhaustion to a pod spec or node label drift issue.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the cluster at the time of re-inspection, the failure may have been caused by a temporary node condition (e.g., node NotReady, taint applied) rather than resource exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create fails on re-run while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime pass, the shared scheduling bottleneck hypothesis is weakened and a check-specific configuration issue should be investigated.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a clear capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.

Add an orphaned-pod cleanup eval that detects remote-agent pods in non-terminal states (Pending, Running) that have exceeded a maximum age, indicating a leaked resource from a prior eval run.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulerMessage) so future failures include the scheduling reason in the evidence object rather than only in the check message.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-17T22:17–22:22Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm; 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote-agent pod to remain Unschedulable for ~146–148 seconds before the eval timeout fires. Because no agent pod was ever scheduled, the runner's createAgent call never returned an agent identity, and the expected evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were never written, producing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents Swarm runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two eligible nodes. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two kata-capable nodes. As a result, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in Unschedulable state, the eval runner's createAgent step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1364) never completes, and no evidence is collected — causing all three remote-agents checks to fail with a contract gap on orgId, agentId, readyState, and state. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption is blocked because no lower-priority pods exist on those nodes (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 nodes are already at kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or nodes were removed/relabeled, this could explain why no fallback scheduling is possible.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning or node failure: one or more kata-capable nodes may have been cordoned, drained, or lost, reducing the effective VM slot pool below the demand level at the time of the eval run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T22:15–22:22Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster has zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads — 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner collected no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), causing every contract assertion to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production-api cluster. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have exhausted their allocatable quota; the remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. With no preemption victims available, the pod remained Unschedulable for ~144–147 seconds until the eval timeout fired. This is a cluster-capacity or node-affinity configuration problem in the production runtime, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of impact to other features or user traffic is present in the supplied packet.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots on the two kata-peerpods-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node label drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the required node labels or taints expected by the remote-agent pod spec, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity problem.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster may not have enough kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes to handle concurrent eval probes plus live workloads, causing resource starvation during peak scheduling windows.

QUATERNARY — Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from a prior run consuming the remaining VM slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) failed on a previous run, orphaned pods may be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and preventing new scheduling.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-17T22:17–22:22Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm; 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote-agent pod to remain Unschedulable for ~146–148 seconds before the eval timeout fires. Because no agent pod was ever scheduled, the runner's createAgent call never returned an agent identity, and the expected evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were never written, producing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents Swarm runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two eligible nodes. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two kata-capable nodes. As a result, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in Unschedulable state, the eval runner's createAgent step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1364) never completes, and no evidence is collected — causing all three remote-agents checks to fail with a contract gap on orgId, agentId, readyState, and state. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption is blocked because no lower-priority pods exist on those nodes (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 nodes are already at kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or nodes were removed/relabeled, this could explain why no fallback scheduling is possible.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning or node failure: one or more kata-capable nodes may have been cordoned, drained, or lost, reducing the effective VM slot pool below the demand level at the time of the eval run.

Cluster node inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots were available and unused at the time of the failure would disprove the exhaustion hypothesis and point instead to a scheduler bug or misconfigured resource requests on the probe pod.

Evidence that the node affinity rules on the remote-agent pod spec were changed to exclude 4 nodes intentionally (e.g., a deliberate topology change) would shift the root cause from exhaustion to affinity misconfiguration.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state at the same timestamp would disprove the shared-capacity exhaustion theory and suggest the runtime check has a unique scheduling constraint not shared by its siblings — however, all three siblings failed, making this unlikely.
